title: 14 February 1876. Two men filed for the telephone on one day.
description:
Two men filed for the telephone on one day. Alexander Graham Bell filed a patent application. Elisha Gray filed a patent caveat.

Filed through his lawyer, William D. Baldwin. By his account, the caveat was taken to the office hours before Bell's papers.

Bell arrived first. Historians still disagree. Bell's fee reached the cash blotter first, but Gray's caveat may have sat unprocessed in the in-basket until the afternoon.

The speed of the paperwork. Bell's lawyer had his fee entered at once. Gray's went through at the usual pace, and reached the examiner the next day.

It reached the Supreme Court. The Telephone Appeals were argued from 24 January to 8 February 1887.

One day, two filings, and a dispute that never fully settled.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Gray_and_Alexander_Bell_telephone_controversy (read): established that Bell's patent application and Gray's caveat were both filed on 14 February 1876; that Gray's lawyer was William D. Baldwin; that the order of arrival is disputed, with Bell's fee on the cash blotter earlier and Gray's caveat possibly delivered earlier but left in the in-basket until the afternoon; that Gray's fee was entered late that afternoon and his caveat reached the examiner the next day; that patent 174,465 went to Bell; and that the Telephone Appeals were argued from 24 January to 8 February 1887 with Chief Justice Waite writing.
- https://www.themarginalian.org/2008/10/20/telephone-invention-controversy/ (read): corroborated the same filing day, that Gray reached the Patent Office a few hours before Bell's lawyer by this account, that Bell's lawyer had his fee entered immediately, and that Gray's went through at the usual pace and reached the examiner the following morning.
